item.title: Royal Navy urged to replace defective Ice Patrol HMS Protector
item.description: The Royal Navy's only ice patrol vessel has been towed into Devonport, reportedly with a double engine failure, raising fresh concerns over how the news will be interpreted by Argentina. HMS Protector fulfils an icebreaking role to monitor the demilitarized Antarctic and support safe navigation for scientific research in challenging conditions.
item.category: Health & Science, Politics, Antarctica, Falkland Islands

item.title: The Falklands dispute threatens Argentina’s bid to join the trans-Pacific trade pact
item.description: The escalating dispute between Argentina and the United Kingdom over the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands has spilled into trade: London, a member of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, has not ruled out using its position to stall Argentina’s bid to join the pact, which requires the consensus of all its members. The British government says Buenos Aires’s conduct raises “very serious questions about its reliability as a partner”.
item.category: Economy, Politics, Argentina, Falkland Islands, International

item.title: Inter-American Court hears case over the April 11, 2002 killings in Caracas
item.description: The Inter-American Court of Human Rights held this week in San José, Costa Rica, the first public hearing in the case over the killings of April 11, 2002 in Caracas, when an opposition march came under gunfire near the Miraflores Palace. Nineteen people died and dozens were wounded that day, in the run-up to the coup that removed then-president Hugo Chávez from power for two days.
